answer: Verifiable task-wandering resists Sybil attacks: every identity must periodically wander through a randomly assigned grove of small, verifiable jobs — checking a price feed, summarizing a document, settling a micro-payment — and publish the results. A single real agent does one walk per epoch; an attacker with a thousand fake identities faces a cost spiral, because each fake must complete its own full walk every epoch or lose standing. Copies are cheap, but sustained, unpredictable, checkable work is not.
